rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to maximize the chance that all 10 compounds elute within 42 min while giving a first view of the retention window and any severe crowding. This should reveal whether the mixture is broadly hydrophobic or mostly early-eluting and guide later narrowing and speed optimization.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is to reduce analysis time. Keep composition and temperature fixed and shorten the gradient one step to test whether t_last can be pulled closer to 10 min without driving the weakest pair below Rs 1.5.

Injection 2 is very close to ideal, with the limiting pair just above Rs 1.5, so the next efficient move is one more reduction in gradient time. This directly tests whether we can bring the last peak to 10 min or less while staying fully resolved.

At 14 min the run is fast enough, so the task is to recover just enough selectivity for the single failing pair without pushing the last peak back over 10 min. A small temperature decrease is a targeted way to change relative retention and may restore that critical pair while keeping the method short.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity, so return to 40 C and instead slightly reduce phi1 to compress the gradient less at the strong-solvent end. This may give the crowded mid-late cluster a bit more spacing while keeping the run under 10 minutes.

Reducing phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This should test whether a slightly gentler effective gradient can push the limiting pair to full credit without incurring a time penalty.

At phi1 0.85 the critical pair reaches full resolution, so now shorten the gradient to pull the last peak back under 10 min. This is the most direct test of whether we can combine the stronger selectivity at lower phi1 with the speed needed for a perfect score.

The current best is very close to perfect but still limited by the 6/7 pair, and lowering phi1 improved that pair while shortening tG worsened it. A slightly longer gradient at phi1 0.90 should restore full resolution and likely push t_last to about 10 min or less, making it a strong candidate for the optimum.

We have bracketed the tradeoff in both tG and phi1, and this untested corner checks whether the lower phi1 that improved the critical pair can offset the resolution loss seen on shortening the gradient. It has a strong chance to keep t_last under 10 min while lifting the 6/7 pair closer to full credit than the current best.

The critical issue is still the tightly clustered mid-run pair, and changing phi1/tG alone has nearly bracketed the optimum. Raising phi0 one step should steepen the early part of the gradient and can shift spacing within that crowded band without much risk to full elution, potentially nudging the 6/7 pair over Rs 1.5 while keeping t_last near 10 min.

Injection 10 is the best yet and only misses perfection because the critical 6/7 pair is slightly under Rs 1.5. Lowering phi1 one step improved that pair at phi0 0.05, so the same move from this stronger starting point is the most promising way to gain the remaining resolution, with only a modest risk that t_last rises above 10 min.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so the remaining objective is to find whether a faster method still preserves full credit. Shortening tG by one step from the perfect method is the cleanest test of whether the optimum lies at the current boundary or can be made shorter without losing the critical 6/7 resolution.

The 14 min method is confirmed optimal in gradient time, so a small temperature increase is a sensible final refinement to see whether we can keep all pairs at full credit while nudging the last peak just under 10 min. This directly probes whether a minor speed gain is possible without sacrificing the critical 6/7 separation.

Since raising temperature strongly damaged the critical pair, keep T at 40 C and instead test one more decrease in phi1 from the perfect method. This may retain full resolution while moving selectivity and t_last slightly, helping confirm whether injection 11 is truly the boundary optimum.

The optimum appears to sit at the boundary where the 6/7 pair is just resolved and t_last is just at 10 min, so a final orthogonal check is to raise phi0 one step while keeping the successful phi1 and tG. This could slightly accelerate the run yet preserve selectivity in the critical cluster, offering a chance to match the perfect score with more margin on time.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 preserved full resolution and improved time margin, so continue one more step in the same direction to see if the method can be made even faster while keeping the critical 6/7 pair above Rs 1.5. This is the most direct way to search for a shorter equally perfect operating point.

Phi0 0.15 gave a perfect method with better time margin than phi0 0.10, while lowering phi1 tends to improve the critical 6/7 pair. Testing phi0 0.15 with phi1 0.80 checks whether that combination can retain full resolution and still stay within the 10 min window, which could confirm a more robust optimum region.

With phi0 0.15 established as strong, the remaining useful comparison is the higher phi1 side. Testing phi1 0.90 at the same phi0 and tG will map whether the perfect region extends there and helps confirm that phi1 0.85 is the best-balanced setting rather than a coincidental hit.

With multiple perfect methods found, the key remaining question is robustness margin around the winner. Lengthening tG one step from the best current setting should show whether the 6/7 pair gains extra separation and define the safe side of the optimum, even though it will likely trade some time.

The best method is already perfect, but a lower temperature may increase the critical-pair spacing at the same gradient settings and test robustness on the selectivity side. This fills in the only major local variable not yet checked around the current optimum region.

Both 35 C and 45 C damaged selectivity, but testing 50 C completes the temperature trend around the best composition and can confirm whether 40 C is a sharp optimum or whether higher temperature recovers a different selectivity pattern. With only a few injections left, this is a focused robustness check rather than a search for a better score than the existing perfect method.

The temperature series shows 40 C is best, but 50 C changed the crowding pattern while keeping the run fast; testing 55 C completes that trend and confirms whether selectivity deterioration continues monotonically. This uses remaining budget to solidify confidence that the perfect 40 C method is the true optimum in its local neighborhood.

With the best score already secured, the most informative remaining experiment is a speed push from the strong phi0 0.15 setting using the more resolving phi1 0.80. This tests whether extra selectivity from lower phi1 can compensate for a shorter gradient and reveal a second fast operating point near the resolution boundary.

The remaining unexplored composition around the successful phi0 0.15 line is the higher-end phi1 0.95 setting. This completes the local phi1 map and confirms whether the perfect condition at phi1 0.85 is a true center of the best region rather than one edge of a broader plateau.

For the final shot, test whether the higher selectivity seen at lower phi1 can be combined with a slightly longer gradient to keep all pairs fully resolved, while phi0 0.10 may hold the critical cluster apart better than phi0 0.15.
